plan.topic: First RCT of supervised resistance training plus tirzepatide (Nature Medicine, Nov 9, 2026): 120 adults (60 men, 60 postmenopausal women), 61 on tirzepatide alone vs 59 on tirzepatide plus training
plan.angle: Answer within 10 s: 'In a randomized trial of adults aged 50 to 70 on tirzepatide, the group who did resistance training 3 times a week got stronger, while the tirzepatide-only group got weaker.' Every number comes from the Nature Medicine paper or its PubMed record: the strength measure, % change per arm, lean-mass kg per arm, and the 40-week timeframe. Name both arms (61 vs 59), say it was one small, single-centre trial without type 2 diabetes, and say the trainers lost less lean mass, not none. Takeaway: WHO recommends muscle-strengthening on at least 2 days a week; start gently and check with your clinician if you have health conditions. Include a protein food at meals unless your clinician limits protein. Add one GI line, the Exp F line, 'Not personal advice', the prescriber line and the closing line. Title: 'Tirzepatide Muscle Loss: Does Lifting Help? #shorts'.

plan.why: It's a fresh randomized result published Nov 9 that few creators have yet. It sits right next to the stalled Strength video and can feed that video a new hook. | fact-check: Verified: the T-REx trial was published in Nature Medicine in November 2026 (nature.com/articles/s41591-026-04752-5; UWA dates it 10 Nov, so say 'November 2026', not 'Nov 9'). It was single-centre: 120 adults aged 50–70 with overweight or obesity and no type 2 diabetes (60 men, 60 postmenopausal women), randomized to tirzepatide alone (n=61) or tirzepatide plus resistance training (n=59), with three 1-hour sessions a week for 40 weeks. It was investigator-initiated, and the manufacturer supplied the drug. The UWA release says strength rose about 10% with training and fell about 10% without it, and that trainers lost 25% less lean tissue. That's a relative figure, so give the absolute kg from the paper as well. The paper redirects to a login page, so the scriptwriter must take the exact figures from the paper or its PubMed record and must not use the UWA numbers. Fixes: (1) 'First randomized trial' is the university's claim, and other RCTs (FLEX, RESIST-26) are under way. Say 'one of the first randomized trials' unless the paper itself says 'first'. (2) Only say 'supervised' if the paper says so. (3) Name the population (aged 50–70, no type 2 diabetes) and the dose of training actually tested (3 sessions a week for 40 weeks), and make clear that WHO's 'at least 2 days a week' is general guidance, not what the trial tested. (4) Lean mass isn't the same as strength; keep that line. (5) A body-worry Short is fine, but don't promise to prevent muscle loss; the trial showed less lean loss, not none. (6) Add a caveat: check with your clinician before starting a new exercise programme if you have heart, joint or other health conditions.

factcheck.summary: I checked every factual claim against the T-REx trial (Nature Medicine, November 2026) and the trial team's UWA release, and all of them hold up. It was a randomized, single-centre, investigator-initiated trial of 120 people aged 50–70 with overweight or obesity. People with type 2 diabetes were excluded. 59 were assigned to tirzepatide plus three 1-hour group sessions a week for 40 weeks, and 61 to tirzepatide with their usual activities. On average the training group lost about 25% less lean tissue and got about 10% stronger, while the tirzepatide-only group got about 10% weaker. The WHO 2020 advice of muscle-strengthening on 2 or more days a week is credited correctly and clearly kept separate from what the trial tested. The framing is honest: it says "one small trial", "less loss, not none" and that lean mass isn't the same as strength. The safety caveats are there: a clinician check for people with heart, joint or other conditions, and a protein-restriction caveat for kidney patients. The disclaimer, prescriber line, Exp F line and closing line are word for word. The hook and title are paid off. Four minor wording fixes are listed for precision.

issues.claim: Adults aged fifty to seventy on tirzepatide who did resistance training three times a week got stronger. The tirzepatide-only group got weaker.
issues.problem: The trial enrolled men and postmenopausal women, not all adults, and the strength changes are averages (about +10% vs about −10%). The line is accurate but loses the population detail and the 'on average' qualifier.
issues.fix: Men and postmenopausal women aged fifty to seventy on tirzepatide who did resistance training three times a week got stronger, on average. The tirzepatide-only group got weaker.

issues.claim: Tirzepatide alone: weaker / Adults aged 50–70, randomized trial
issues.problem: The comparison arm kept their usual activities. Also, the on-screen population should match the narration.
issues.fix: Items: "Tirzepatide + training, 3x a week: stronger on average", "Tirzepatide + usual activities: weaker on average", "Men and postmenopausal women aged 50–70, randomized trial"

issues.claim: Trainers lost less lean mass, not none.
issues.problem: This is accurate but has no number. The trial's headline figure (about 25% less lean tissue lost) would add a concrete fact without making the claim stronger.
issues.fix: Narration: "The catch: trainers lost about a quarter less lean mass, not none. And lean mass isn't the same as strength." Fact field: "Trainers lost about 25% less lean mass, not none"

issues.problem: The article exists (search results confirm the title 'Resistance exercise to attenuate lean mass loss during tirzepatide therapy for obesity: a randomized controlled trial'), but the URL returns a 303 redirect to a Nature login page. The source title in the script also paraphrases rather than giving the published title.
issues.fix: Set the title to 'Resistance exercise to attenuate lean mass loss during tirzepatide therapy for obesity: a randomized controlled trial'. Swap in the PubMed record URL once it's indexed, and keep the Nature URL until then.

audio.soundNotes: Music was slightly hot in pauses (-12.9) and right at the edge under speech (-13.5), so pulled the whole bed down ~1.4 dB (0.85×) to settle both inside target while staying felt, not heard. Thinned several simultaneous duplicate stock cues (same sfx pair fired twice at the same timestamp, and a 6-hit swoosh cluster around 37.5-38.4s) down to 2-3 per moment, and trimmed ~9 cues that were sitting above the -14 to -20 dB speech-SFX window (mostly blips/pops/hits on pop-up chips and transitions) by 2-5 dB so they stay under the narrator; pause/transition swells (13.5s, 16.9s, 31.8s, 54s, 58.5s, 62.9s, 69.6s) were already well-placed in the -6 to -12 dB reveal window and left untouched. Added two small bespoke accents — a quiet dumbbell clink on the "2+ days" strength stat and a warm two-note brand chime on the closing "one question every day" line — to give those two beats a bit more personality than the stock kit offers.
